caller.persona: worried {{c_mother}} trying to stay level, voice cracking at the edges, over-explaining
caller.openingLine: Hi, um, I don't know if this is the right thing but my {{p_son}} hasn't come home from school and it's been four hours and {{p_his}} phone's going straight to voicemail and that's just not her, she always answers me.
dontKnowLines: I don't know. God, I should know that, shouldn't I.
I don't know, I've been ringing everyone.

incident.summaryTruth: {{callerName}} reports {{c_his}} {{p_son}} {{patientName}}, {{patientAge}}, has not returned from Boundstone College, {{town}}. Last seen leaving school at 3:15pm by a friend, four hours ago. Phone off or dead, going straight to voicemail. No argument at home. {{patientFirst}} is described as white, 5ft 3, shoulder-length dyed red hair, school uniform with a black puffer coat, black rucksack. No previous missing episodes. Best friend Amelia has not seen {{p_him}} since the school gate. {{patientFirst}} recently mentioned an an older {{p_boy}} {{p_he}} met online, name not known she met online, mother does not know his surname, this had caused mild concern. Caller is at home at {{address}}, {{town}} with her younger son.

facts.label: Last confirmed sighting
facts.beat: Her friend saw her walking out the school gates at quarter past three. Boundstone College. Nobody's seen {{p_him}} since, that's four hours.

facts.label: Description
facts.value: white, 5ft 3, dyed red hair, school uniform, black puffer coat, black rucksack
facts.beat: She's five foot three, slim, her hair's dyed red, shoulder length. School uniform, and a black puffer coat, black rucksack.

facts.label: Phone status
facts.beat: Straight to voicemail every time since about four. It's never off. Even when she's sulking she reads the messages.

facts.label: Concerning online contact
facts.value: an older {{p_boy}} {{p_he}} met online, name not known, met online
facts.beat: There's... she mentioned a boy called Connor a few weeks back. Older. She met him online, I never got a surname. I told her I didn't like it. You don't think...

facts.label: Previous episodes
facts.beat: Never. Not once. That's why I'm ringing you and not just waiting.

facts.label: Argument at home
facts.beat: No, nothing. This morning was completely normal, she had her toast, {{p_he}} was singing in the bathroom.

escalations.text: Member of public reports a girl matching the description sat alone at Worthing pier shelter, matching black puffer coat and red hair.
